newsitem.title: JAPAN: Exporters' sales weigh on dollar vs yen in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Exporters' sales weigh on dollar vs yen in Tokyo.

text.p: *Dollar drifted lower against yen in early Tokyo on Monday, dragged down by sales from exporters and speculative sales from interbank operators, dealers said.
*Stop-loss selling orders placed around 113.50 yen, but dealers unlikely to liquidate dollar holdings aggressively.

*"Light dollar sales by exporters were spotted this morning. Interbank operators also unwound their long positions on speculation that the greenback will be capped on offers by exporters and investors," a Japanese city bank dealer said.
*Dollar closed at 113.98/03 yen and 1.7768/78 marks in New York on Friday.
*Technical sales pushed down dollar against mark from early highs in early morning, but undertone of mark stayed weak.

*"It's difficult to determine whether the mark will face further downward pressure in the short term, but the dollar/mark is likely to test 1.7850 again," a trust bank dealer said. "The sentiment of the mark is weak."
*Dollar rose as high as 1.7850 marks in New York on Friday after German currency fell to 3.0 marks against sterling, its lowest since October 1990.
*At 0027 GMT, sterling stood at 3.0046/56 marks, compared with 3.0090/00 marks in early Asian trade.
*Dealers said market will be watching two-day Bank of Japan (BOJ branch managers' meeting, starting today, for clues to economy and interest rate outlook.
*BOJ Governor Yasuo Matsushita's opening speech at branch managers' meeting scheduled for 0130 GMT.
*Dollar/yen rate expected to stay in tight boxed range until trade figures from both United States and Japan are released later on during week. Dealers forecast range of 112 to 115 yen for the week.
*Dealers to close watch how uncertainty in Asian currencies will affect yen. They are focusing on Thai baht and Philippine peso in particular.
*At 0039 GMT, mark stood at 63.90/95 yen, compared with 64.15 yen in New York on Friday.
*Fall of mark to around 63.70 yen, a near two-year low reached last week, could intensify selling pressure and drag German currency down near 63.00 yen.
